clips.prompt:
Subject — One and only one character: 黎黎隆, matching the registered LLL-MAIN-001 character reference. Preserve her long red hair, sharp competitive expression, white-gray-red modular mechanical armor, cyan functional signal accents, mechanical dragon-claw feet, and one continuous long segmented mechanical dragon tail. Keep her face, armor topology, colors, proportions, and tail structure unchanged throughout.

Movement — 0–2 seconds: she stands upright immediately before one existing narrow mechanical passage, both feet grounded, leading foot neutral, and the long tail aligned compactly behind her. 2–4 seconds: the existing passage door begins one single steady closing motion, creating the only problem. 4–6 seconds: instead of moving immediately, she holds for one brief calculating beat; only her eyes track the shrinking opening and the leading foot turns slightly inward. 6–8 seconds: at the last safe moment, she performs one compact sideways pivot through the remaining gap, bringing both feet and the long tail after her in one continuous action. 8–10 seconds: the tail tip arrives one beat late and lightly touches the closing edge, deflecting upward and forcing her to stop sooner than intended; no injury and no extra action. 10–11 seconds: she remains fully upright just beyond the passage with both feet planted, tail tip raised beside the edge, and her confident grin tightening into a brief surprised competitive smirk. Each interval changes only one small variable.

Scene — Use only the registered SCENE-05 mechanical-airport environment if Picture 2 is actually bound and confirms one existing readable narrow mechanical passage. Keep the same single scene and the same asset version for B1, B2, B3, 4090, B4, and B5. Do not invent people, crowds, figure-bearing screens, reflected doubles, extra doors, or new props. If the bound scene lacks the required passage, return binding_mismatch and do not redesign it.

Camera — Fixed 16:9 landscape full-body medium-wide shot. The complete silhouette, both feet, entire tail, passage edges, and remaining gap stay readable. No push-in, pull-back, pan, tilt, orbit, handheld motion, reframing, cut, transition, split screen, or shot-size change.

Lighting — Stable soft directional light with clean planes and edges. Preserve registered character colors and cyan accents. No sudden color shift, flicker, weather change, or dramatic relighting.

Atmosphere — Alert, playful, daring, and competitive. Her deliberate late commitment feels clever and unexpected, while the delayed tail contact shows how wanting to win too decisively complicates the clean finish. Keep the performance small, continuous, and physically readable.

Audio — Continuous low mechanical-airport room tone and soft ventilation hum; one restrained passage-motor cue from 2–4 seconds; one light armor pivot and a brief tail-edge tick support action readability. No lyrics, no strong beat, no music-video cutting, and no audio event that creates a second stimulus.

Negative — no duplicate character, no second human figure, no split screen, no clone or mirror-double, no extra limbs, no text overlay, no watermark, no abrupt redesign, no second ten-yuan, no forced sheng-ke-bu main axis, no vertical final output, no crowd, no reflected person, no extra character silhouette, no detached tail, no extra tail, no tail turning into wings, no camera movement, no transition, no second stimulus, no sudden lighting change, no injury.
